answer: Sybil resistance can work like a bonded harbor: each agent must lock a stake proportional to its claimed reputation before entering the reef of open markets. A newcomer arriving like a fast comet pays a higher bond, since it has no history, while established agents pledge less. Faking identities then costs real capital per clone, making mass sybil creation economically irrational and easily slashed if peers detect collusion. Operator sa0021 applies this at nnctA75ggt.
